prediction_ref.short_label: Selective-expert-checkpointing lands as default MoE save primitive by H2 2026

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Today's own prediction lands directly on the Unsloth v2026.5.26 release. The tagged point release introduces a selective-expert-checkpoint primitive that freezes inactive expert columns on disk during checkpoint write, collapsing the MiniMax M2.7 235B MoE port's checkpoint footprint from roughly 470GB to 188GB across the first ten saved revisions. The paired Daniel Han Chen and Mike Han Chen Hugging Face Blog benchmark sheet reports Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B training at ~1.74x throughput versus the prior DeepSeek R3-Pro 38B recipe under the same router-only LoRA driver on a single 8x H200 SXM5 node, with peak combined VRAM down 11.3 percent against a vanilla Hugging Face Transformers v5 baseline. Two independent reproductions on CoreWeave and Crusoe Cloud 8x H200 SXM5 rentals landed inside 3 percent of the published numbers within the trading day, and a Simon Willison note flagged the primitive as the most operationally meaningful change shipped this quarter for downstream fine-tuners running against SSD budget caps on Lambda Labs or RunPod. The release also lifts the contributed 60B-class recipe count to four with a Tsinghua KEG Lab MiniMax M2.7 port joining the existing DeepSeek R3-Pro, OLMo-2 60B, and Qwen3 MoE 60B set.

prediction_ref.short_label: SEC extends 8-K cyber materiality to agentic-AI dev-tool incidents by Q3 2026

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Today's own prediction lands directly on the CISA KEV listing of CVE-2026-46127. GitHub Security Lab disclosed a critical-severity (CVSS 9.4) prompt-injection-escalation vulnerability in OpenAI's open-source Codex CLI v3.1.x development branch in which an attacker can chain a workspace-scoped sandboxed Codex agent into an unsandboxed shell-exec context via a crafted MCP-server response that exploits a missing JSON-Schema validation step in the agent harness's tool-call deserialization path. The Hacker News reported CISA placed CVE-2026-46127 on its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog inside the same Tuesday window after a Mandiant incident-response engagement at a Fortune 500 financial-services customer confirmed active exploitation in the wild, and OpenAI's Tuesday security note stated the production-tier auto-update path will force-roll all v3.1.x development tenants to v3.1.10 inside a 72-hour window. NIST NVD published a Tuesday afternoon update confirming the CVSS 9.4 scoring and reclassifying the vulnerability under the agent-loader subcategory, lifting the Trail of Bits agentic-AI tooling-stack CVE taxonomy to twelve catalogued instances (the first net-new since the May 8 cycle).
